_note: Thomas, 2026-09-06: 'chase all of the round 3 leads'. The corpus carried no UK census statute at all — an odd gap next to Australia's Census and Statistics Act 1905 (minted in round 2), Ireland's Statistics Act 1993 and the UK's own Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007. Every UK census runs on a two-step statutory chain: a permanent Census Act, plus a Census Order made afresh for each census. This slice mints both steps for all three UK census jurisdictions and wires the three census nodes to them. Every edge is A, and each rests on two independent readings: the census publisher's own document naming the instrument by title, and the instrument's own enacting recital. Northern Ireland is a separate legal system and section 10(2) of the 1920 Act says so verbatim ('This Act shall not extend to Ireland'), so nir-census-2021 hangs off the Census Act (Northern Ireland) 1969 instead — a distinction that would have been easy to get wrong. Every url and evidence_url was raw-verified HTTP 200 and every quote re-fetched and substring-checked against the live cited URL after this file was written.

reports.title: Census Act 1920
reports.description: The permanent statute authorising the taking of a census in Great Britain. Section 1(1) provides that it is lawful for His Majesty by Order in Council from time to time to direct that a census be taken for Great Britain or any part of it, and that such an Order may prescribe the census date, the persons by and about whom returns are made, and the particulars to be stated. Section 2(1), as amended by the Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007, places the duty to carry out the census on the Statistics Board in relation to England and Wales and on the Registrar General for Scotland in relation to Scotland. Section 10(2) provides that the Act does not extend to Ireland, so it is not the basis for the Northern Ireland census.
reports.cadence_note: Section 1(1) proviso (i) sets a minimum interval, not a fixed decennial requirement: an Order may not require a census in any part of Great Britain in a year unless at least five years have elapsed since the year the last census was taken there.

reports.title: The Census (England and Wales) Order 2020
reports.publisher: His Majesty in Council, on the recommendation of the Minister for the Cabinet Office
reports.description: The Order in Council directing Census 2021 in England and Wales (SI 2020 No. 532), made 20 May 2020. It recites that it is made in exercise of the powers conferred by section 1(1) of the Census Act 1920, following consultation with the Welsh Ministers. Article 2 defines census day as 21 March 2021 and article 3 directs that a census is to be taken for England and Wales on that date; article 4(3) requires returns in the form prescribed by regulations made under section 3 of the Act.

reports.title: The Census (Scotland) Order 2020
reports.publisher: His Majesty in Council, approved by resolution of the Scottish Parliament
reports.description: The Order in Council directing Scotland's census (SSI 2020 No. 76), made 11 March 2020 and extending to Scotland only. It recites that it is made under sections 1(1) and 8(1A)(b) of the Census Act 1920 and was approved by resolution of the Scottish Parliament. As made it set census day at 21 March 2021; the Census (Scotland) Amendment Order 2020 (SSI 2020/436, made 16 December 2020) substituted 20 March 2022 in both article 2 and article 3, so this Order as amended is the operative directing instrument for Scotland's Census 2022.

reports.title: Census Act (Northern Ireland) 1969
reports.description: The permanent statute authorising the census in Northern Ireland, which is a separate legal system from Great Britain — the Census Act 1920 expressly does not extend to it. Section 1(1), as amended, provides that the First Minister and deputy First Minister acting jointly may by order direct that a census of population be taken in Northern Ireland, and section 1(4) requires a draft of that order to be laid before and approved by resolution of the Assembly. Section 2(2) names the Registrar General for Northern Ireland as the officer who must make the arrangements for taking a census.
reports.cadence_note: Section 1(3)(a) sets the same five-year minimum interval as the 1920 Act: an order may not require a census in Northern Ireland in a year unless at least five years have elapsed since the year the last one was taken.

reports.title: The Census Order (Northern Ireland) 2020
reports.publisher: The First Minister and deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland
reports.description: The statutory rule directing Census 2021 in Northern Ireland (SR 2020 No. 83), laid before the Assembly in draft, made 5 May 2020 and in operation from 6 May 2020. Its opening recital states that the First Minister and deputy First Minister acting jointly make the Order under section 1(1) of the Census Act (Northern Ireland) 1969. Article 2 defines census day as 21 March 2021 and article 3 directs that a census be taken for Northern Ireland on that date; its Schedule lists the topics for the census questionnaire.

_dropped.why: DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED 2026-09-06, and recorded so it is not derived by analogy later. Section 10(2) of the Census Act 1920 says verbatim: 'This Act shall not extend to Ireland.' Section 1(1) confines the power to 'Great Britain, or ... any part of Great Britain'. Northern Ireland is a separate legal system and its census runs on the Census Act (Northern Ireland) 1969, which this round minted. The obvious-looking edge from the NI census to the UK-wide Act would be wrong.
